About this motion illustration

Prescribed kinematics, not a force or contact simulation. Actuator movement replays a nominal clearance calculation; timing, friction and tooth engagement are not simulated. Continuous powered output rotation is not animated. The viewer sequences the controls for you; the real build requires the write sequence below.

Seated stack — actual frame coordinates
Printed frameOpen retaining framesCarriages / integral linksRockersHOLD lock linkageLEGO bearing inserts
D / BUSOne shared data axle. Turn it to load; the bit drives it only when OE = 1.
W · Write1 releases the holding bolt and admits data. 0 disconnects data and locks the completed state.
OE · Output enable1 connects the stored value to the bus. 0 leaves the bus free for another writer.
P · PowerContinuous clockwise drive supplies the stored output. The internal Q shaft is inverted.

A complete first-bit demonstrator

The data actuator stops during HOLD. The two command actuators still overrun at their endpoints while their command axles keep turning. Return bands bias the rockers; they do not transmit torque by slipping.

Printing, operation and parts →

Write completely, then lock

Disable OE. Establish a stable data direction. Assert W until the carriage has fully seated; return W to 0 while keeping data stable. Only then change the bus or enable output. Releasing W midway through a stroke is outside the permitted write sequence.

All input directions are viewed from the negative-X end, looking along the axle: clockwise = 0, counterclockwise = 1. A disconnected bus is neither 0 nor 1.

Actual native LEGO meshes and exported printed solids. Playback is a prescribed illustration, not a dynamic contact simulation. Do not print the combined inspection assembly. Use the individual millimetre STLs and fit coupon; no maximum speed, load rating or eight-bit endurance is claimed.
